expected.tagline: Explore Kanto with a pickaxe and a hotbar.
expected.description: An unofficial browser fan game that brings mining, crafting and block placement to a Pokémon adventure. Move with WASD or the arrow keys, mine with Z, and use X to place the item in your hand.

installSteps.text: Open the official Pokémon Redstone browser page.
Click the game area to give it keyboard focus.
Use the arrow keys or WASD to move and Z to mine or interact.
Press E for inventory and select an item from the hotbar before using X.
Use Enter for the menu or J for the map.

Do I need an account to play Pokémon Redstone?
faq.a: You can download and play without creating an account.
No. Pokémon Redstone is a single-player game, so there is no multiplayer mode to join or host.

set.tagline: Kanto has a hotbar now, and the flowers are about to find out.
set.description: An unofficial browser fan game that drops a block-building adventurer into Kanto. Explore, mine, place blocks, craft and encounter familiar creatures. It plays in a modern browser, accepts keyboard, touch and native gamepad input, and offers a four-player room-code co-op mode.

systemRequirements.min: A current browser with JavaScript, Canvas 2D and WebAudio enabled. No desktop executable or fixed disk installation is published. The developer has not posted CPU, RAM or GPU minimums.
systemRequirements.recommended: A current desktop browser with a keyboard or compatible Gamepad API controller and a reliable connection for room-code co-op. No numerical recommended PC specification is published.

min.notes: Browser game; no local installer. A modern JavaScript/Canvas browser is required. The developer has not published CPU, GPU or RAM minimums. Mobile touch input also exists, outside this desktop hardware schema.

recommended.notes: Use a current browser and reliable connection for co-op. Gamepad input uses the browser Gamepad API. No numerical CPU/GPU/RAM target is published.

qualityBar.verdict: It turns the familiar first walk through Kanto into a quiet temptation to dismantle the scenery and build something of your own.

set.longDescription:
Pokémon Redstone starts with an impossible crossover and then makes it surprisingly literal. Instead of simply dressing an old map with new sprites, it gives a block-building adventurer tools to mine, place, craft and reshape the world of Kanto. The first familiar town becomes less of a route marker and more of a place to inspect. Can you move that block? What happens if you dig here? Is the grass still just grass when your inventory has a hotbar? Those are good questions for a fan project to make you ask before it has even sent you toward the next city.

The live browser build uses familiar keyboard ideas: arrows or WASD to move, Z to mine, attack or talk, X to use, place or eat, Space to jump, Shift to sprint and E for inventory. A hotbar and block systems sit alongside creature encounters and menus inspired by the source games. The result is more of a playful collision between two sets of habits than a straight remake. You recognize a house and a road, but you are carrying a tool that changes how you treat both. The game gives you room to wander rather than reducing the whole idea to a single joke about a pickaxe.

It also has multiplayer. The title screen offers JOIN CO-OP, and the current client code uses four room slots, one for the host and three for guests. Players join by room code and name; the host's world is the shared world. That is direct in-game online co-op, not a dedicated-server download or a virtual LAN setup. PlayBound can organize friends and pass along a room code, but no automatic party-to-game join handoff has been verified yet. The browser build has native gamepad polling through the Gamepad API, mapping its buttons into the same logical actions as the keyboard, and it also has touch input. That is more support than the old Draft record showed, though a complete physical-controller session on PlayBound still deserves testing.

This is an unofficial fan project credited on its own page to mozetech. Its title screen explicitly says it is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Game Freak, Mojang or Microsoft. PlayBound should show that context clearly. It is free to play at the developer's browser URL; there is no downloadable Windows, Mac or Linux installer to promise. The developer does not publish numerical CPU, GPU or RAM requirements. A current browser with JavaScript and Canvas support is the honest minimum, and co-op benefits from a stable connection.

We captured the game's own title art and two in-world frames for this listing, including a view of Pallet Town. The project stays Draft while we test the room-code path, gamepad behavior and longer session stability. The hook is already visible in the first few seconds: Kanto looks like a place you remember, until you realize you are allowed to pick up the scenery.
set.whyWePickedIt: The developer went further than a visual mash-up: block interaction, Kanto exploration, native browser gamepad input and four-player co-op make the idea playable. Its unofficial status and the untested PlayBound party handoff remain clearly stated.
set.thatOneThing: You reach Pallet Town with a hotbar and immediately start wondering whether the route's tidy landscaping is mineable.

installSteps.text: Open the developer's Pokémon Redstone page in a modern browser. There is no local installer or game file download to run through PlayBound.
Choose Press Start for a solo world, or Join Co-op and enter a friend's room code. Keyboard, touch and browser Gamepad API input are available in the live build.

firstPlaySteps.text: Use arrows/WASD to move, Z to mine or talk, X to use or place, Space to jump and E for inventory. The in-game Controls screen shows the full binding list. If using a pad, connect it before opening or reloading the browser page.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: A host starts a co-op world in the browser and shares its room code. Up to three guests join through the title screen's Join Co-op option, for four players total. PlayBound's party can coordinate the group, but automatic room-code handoff has not been verified.

faq.a: Yes. It runs on the developer's public website without a game download or purchase.

faq.q: Is it an official Pokémon or Minecraft game?
faq.a: No. The developer describes it as an unofficial fan project and disclaims affiliation with Nintendo, Game Freak, Mojang and Microsoft.
Yes. The live browser build has a room-code co-op mode with one host and up to three guests. PlayBound automatic joining is not yet verified.
The browser client polls Gamepad API controllers and maps them to its game actions. PlayBound has not yet completed a full controller session test.
The developer has not published numerical PC specifications. Use a current browser with JavaScript and Canvas enabled; there is no separate installed game footprint.

bestFor: Players who enjoy exploring familiar maps in unexpected ways
Friends who want a small free browser co-op experiment
notFor: Players seeking an officially licensed Pokémon release
Players who need a native offline installer or dedicated server
